FINDING_ID: R3_FSM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
DESCRIPTION: `RoundProgressionFSM.select_event()` can return `Event.MAX` from the final iterative round even when `Event.DIMINISHED` is also valid and higher priority by the documented ordering. The method checks `diminished` before `round_complete`, but inside the `round_complete` branch it unconditionally returns `MAX` for `ROUND_{N-1}`. This makes `MAX` effectively outrank `COMPLETE`, but also lets completion-path logic mask the semantic distinction between “stopped because max rounds reached” and “stopped because diminishing returns detected at the final round” whenever callers set `round_complete=True` after evaluating stop predicates in a different order or reuse the selected event downstream. The priority contract says `FAIL_CRITICAL > CONVERGED > DIMINISHED > COMPLETE > MAX`; current logic implements `FAIL_CRITICAL > CONVERGED > DIMINISHED > (MAX as special case of round_complete) > COMPLETE`, which is not the same machine. This is subtle but important because termination reason drives reporting and policy.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make `MAX` an independently selected event only when no higher-priority stop event applies and the machine is in `ROUND_{N-1}`. Concretely, move final-round `MAX` handling out of the `round_complete` branch into its own lower-priority branch after `COMPLETE`, or define a single explicit priority table over valid events and choose the max-ranked applicable event from that set.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R3_FSM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: `RoundProgressionFSM.transition(Event.COMPLETE)` from `SYNTH` always creates `ROUND_1`, regardless of whether iterative rounds exist. Prior finding ChatGPT_F017 covered the `select_event()` path for `max_rounds == 1`, but the deeper issue is that the state transition function itself violates the declared state space invariant. The docstring says states are `{BLIND, SYNTH, ROUND_1, ..., ROUND_{N-1}, TERMINAL}` and terminates in at most `N + 2` transitions. For `max_rounds == 1`, the valid state space should contain no `ROUND_k` states at all because `N-1 = 0`. Yet `transition()` manufactures `ROUND_1` even if called directly or by any future caller that bypasses `select_event()`. This means the FSM is not self-validating; one helper has the bug, but the core transition relation also encodes an impossible state.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Guard the `SYNTH` + `COMPLETE` transition with `if self.max_round_idx < 1: raise ValueError(...)` or transition directly to `TERMINAL` with `MAX_ROUNDS` if the design intends `SYNTH` to be the last executable stage when no iterative rounds exist. Also add an invariant test that all produced states belong to the configured state space.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R3_FSM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68  
DESCRIPTION: The validator methods are not configuration-safe and can fail spuriously for legitimate edge configurations. `validate_k1()` assumes `ROUND_1` exists and hardcodes `BLIND -> SYNTH -> ROUND_1 -> TERMINAL`, while `validate_no_failures()` assumes `Event.MAX` is reachable after entering `ROUND_1`. For `max_rounds <= 1`, these validators either assert impossible states or drive invalid transitions. That makes the advertised reduction/property checks unreliable exactly at boundary conditions where they should be strongest. This is separate from the runtime FSM bug: even if transition logic were fixed, the validators still encode a narrower model than the config allows.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rewrite validators against the formal configured state space. For example, compute the expected chain from `max_round_idx`; if there are zero iterative rounds, validate `BLIND -> SYNTH -> TERMINAL` or whatever the intended semantics are. Avoid hardcoded `ROUND_1` assumptions.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R3_FSM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: The FSM’s own documentation is internally inconsistent about what `max_rounds` means. `max_round_idx` is documented as “Maximum iterative round index (N-1),” implying `max_rounds = N`. But `__post_init__` sets `current_round = 0  # BLIND = round 0`, and validators/toplevel comments talk about “at most N + 2 transitions” as if BLIND/SYNTH are outside the iterative count. This ambiguity leaks into implementation bugs around `max_rounds == 1`. The issue is not merely wording: the machine cannot be reasoned about correctly if “rounds” sometimes include BLIND and sometimes only iterative rounds.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Define one canonical interpretation in code comments and names. If `max_rounds` means total executed rounds including BLIND and SYNTH, rename/add derived properties accordingly. If it means iterative rounds only, then set bounds and validators from that meaning consistently and stop using `current_round=0` for BLIND unless separately named `stage_index`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R3_FSM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60  
DESCRIPTION: `current_round` is not a faithful projection of `current_state`; it is partially updated and therefore can become stale or misleading for consumers. On initialization it is `0` for BLIND. After `BLIND -> SYNTH`, it remains `0`. After terminal transitions (`CONVERGED`, `DIMINISHED`, `MAX`, `FAIL_CRITICAL`), it is not updated at all. This means a terminal FSM may report `current_state == TERMINAL` with `current_round == 0` or `1` depending on where it stopped, but callers cannot tell whether that number is “last completed round,” “current active round,” or “most recent iterative round.” That ambiguity is dangerous because orchestration and metrics code often key storage by round index. A stale round index next to a terminal state invites off-by-one writes and misleading summaries.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace `current_round` with explicitly named fields such as `last_completed_round`, `active_round`, or `stage_index`, and update them on every transition by derivation from state. At minimum, document exact semantics and set terminal-round metadata explicitly when transitioning to `TERMINAL`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R3_FSM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: The FSM lacks an explicit invariant checker for acyclicity and monotone forward progress despite claiming to be a “deterministic acyclic FSM” with bounded transitions. `history` is recorded, but no method verifies that each transition strictly advances along the configured linear order or that terminality is absorbing except via the runtime guard. Given the mixed string/enum representation and boundary bugs already present, the absence of a first-class invariant check means structural regressions can slip through while unit tests still pass on happy paths.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a private `_state_rank()` and assert on every transition that `rank(new_state) > rank(old_state)` unless terminal absorption is in effect. Also add a `validate_structure()` helper that enumerates all states/events for a config and checks determinism, legality, and bounded path length.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R3_FSM_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.54  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52  
DESCRIPTION: `valid_events()` reparses round indices from state strings (`int(s.split("_")[1])`) each time rather than deriving validity from a normalized state representation. This is not just stylistic duplication. Because `current_state` is free-form `str`, any accidental corruption to a malformed value like `"ROUND_X"` or `"ROUND_01_EXTRA"` will surface as a low-level parsing exception inside event computation rather than as a clean state-invariant violation. That weakens fault isolation in the orchestration path. Prior finding CC2_F013 noted mixed enum/string typing; the missed issue here is the lack of defensive validation at the parse boundary.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Centralize state parsing in a helper like `_round_index_from_state()` that validates format and raises a domain-specific error, or use a structured representation `(kind, index)` instead of raw strings.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: R3_FSM_X001  
SEVERITY: 0.49  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: Cross-component concern, unverified from this area alone: `DynamicManager.process_round()` likely records and indexes round outputs using external `round_idx` values while the FSM separately maintains `current_round` with BLIND/SYNTH special handling. If the manager treats `process_round()` calls as one-to-one with FSM state transitions, the fact that `SYNTH` shares `current_round == 0` with `BLIND` creates a plausible overwrite or misattribution hazard for round-scoped metrics/history. A prior unverified Gemini finding points in this direction; the FSM design here does not refute it and in fact makes it plausible.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Audit manager-round indexing against FSM stage semantics. Use a single canonical stage/round identifier propagated through `RoundResult`, convergence detectors, and history maps. Distinguish BLIND, SYNTH, and iterative rounds explicitly rather than overloading integer `0`.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

Definitive stance: the strongest new issues in this area are the core transition bug for `max_rounds == 1`, the priority/termination-reason inconsistency around `MAX`, and the ambiguous `current_round` semantics. These are real FSM defects, not just style concerns.
